subject: general
question: Walking at (3)/(4) of this usual speed, a man covers a certain distance in 1 hour and 40 minutes more than the time he takes to cover the distance at his usual speed. The time taken (in hours) by him to cover the same distance at his usual speed is:
solution:
Given:

Walking at (3)/(4) of this usual speed, a man covers a certain distance in 1 hour and 40 minutes more than the time he takes to cover the distance at his usual speed. 

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

1 hour 40 minutes = (1 + 40/60) hours

⇒ (1 + 2/3) = 5/3 hours

Let the usual speed and distance be Q km/h and D km respectively.

Time taken to cover the distance in usual speed = D/Q hours

According to the question,

D/(3Q/4) - D/Q = 5/3

⇒ 4D/3Q - D/Q = 5/3

⇒ D/Q × 1/3 = 5/3

⇒ D/Q = 5

**∴ The time taken by him to cover the same distance at his usual speed is 5 hours.**
